subject: PayGrid — recap: models, eval pack, stability safeguard
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@paygrid.com>, Tom Scully <tom.scully@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Fit signals and suggested evals — PayGrid integration

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned on model fit and how to validate in your environment.

TL;DR
- Recommended candidates: redwood-mistral-7B-v2 (cost-efficient generation), flan-ul2-xxl (high-precision classification for compliance checks).
- I attached an eval pack with 250 representative prompts, expected outputs, and scoring rubric.
- Proposed immediate safeguard: snapshot current serving model and be prepared to pin back to the pre-upgrade snapshot if we see quality regressions after any model/version swap.

What we heard from PayGrid on the call
- High priority: candidate-generation precision for account matching and regulatory phrasing (low false-positive tolerance).
- Volume profile: ~120k calls/day with peaks for reconciliation at EOD; average target latency <= 250ms for single-turn generation.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer smaller, quantized variants for bulk inference; use larger models only for verification paths.

Redwood recommendations
1) Baseline evaluation (short window): run the attached eval pack against two variants — redwood-mistral-7B-v2 and flan-ul2-xxl — and collect the 3-point rubric we discussed (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency).
2) Prompt set: we’ve included a suggested promptset (promptset-paygrid-v2.jsonl) tuned for reconciliation and regulatory wording.
3) Observability: enable token-level cost logging + per-route latency SLOs in the Console for the test runs.
4) Safeguard: if you plan to upgrade the model in production, we’ll snapshot the current version (snap id: pre-prod-20261012) and hold it for 7 days as a rollback target. If automated evals show a >5% degradation on key prompts, we can apply an emergency pin.

Attachments
- paygrid-eval-pack-v1.zip (eval prompts, rubric, runners)
- promptset-paygrid-v2.jsonl

Links
- Eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals
- Deal in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/PG-26-014

Next steps (I suggest):
- PayGrid: confirm the set of 50 priority prompts to run first (can reuse items in the zip).
- Redwood: we’ll spin a short evaluation job against the two variants, deliver a short scorecard within 48 hours, and propose a pin/rollback threshold.
- Quick sync: 30m on Wednesday to review the initial scorecard — propose 10:30am PT.

If helpful, we can also provide a cost delta estimate for the two model choices (rough per-1M tokens cost).

Thanks — I’ll queue the runner once you confirm the priority prompt list.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.com]

[Attachment: paygrid-eval-pack-v1.zip]
[Attachment: promptset-paygrid-v2.jsonl]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Fit signals and suggested evals — PayGrid integration

Jonas / Rishi,

Quick internal note before we go live with the eval run — flagging operational guardrails I want in place:

1) Snapshot + immutable tag: create a snapshot of their current prod variant (pre-prod-20261012) and publish an immutable tag we can revert to.
2) Automated diff harness: run the eval pack and generate a model-diff CSV (attached) that shows per-prompt deltas on accuracy and hallucination flags. Threshold to watch: >5% accuracy drop OR any high-severity hallucination on the compliance prompt group triggers auto-alert.
3) Pin process: if the automation hits the threshold, we do an emergency pin to the snapshot for a 72-hour containment window while ops triages.
4) Communication: ops should notify PayGrid + their CS lead within 30 mins of pinning and open an incident in PagerDuty if SLA degrading.

Estimating slack for rollback: assuming a pin is needed, we can execute within ~10 minutes (snapshot restore + routing change). Data retention / logs will be preserved for the 7-day hold window.

I attached a mock diff to show the kind of CSV output we’ll share: model-diff-20261013.csv.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: model-diff-20261013.csv]

1) Cost / performance: can you send an estimated cost delta (per 1M tokens) between the two suggested variants, and a rough latency profile for our volume?
2) Pinning SLA: if we do an emergency pin back to the pre-prod snapshot, how will that affect in-flight requests and ongoing batched jobs? Any user-facing rollback noise we should warn our ops about?

Also, can we do the Wed 10:30am PT sync — Tom and I can make that. If you can share the HubSpot/Drive links in the calendar invite, that’d be great.

Elena

Elena / Tom — thanks for the quick reply and for committing to the 50 priority prompts. A few concrete notes answering your questions and next steps: 

1) Cost & latency (rough estimates)
- redwood-mistral-7B-v2: ~ $45 / 1M tokens; median p95 latency ~ 180–240ms on our dedicated 8xA10 pool for your payload size.
- flan-ul2-xxl: ~ $180 / 1M tokens; median p95 latency ~ 320–420ms.
We’ll publish a more precise run-based estimate after the initial 50-prompt run.

2) Pin/rollback behavior
- In-flight requests: we gracefully drain existing workers during the routing flip; in-flight requests are allowed to finish, new requests route to the pinned snapshot. Expect a <5% transient rate of elevated latency for requests hitting draining workers.
- Batched jobs: we recommend pausing non-critical batch jobs for the 10–15 minute window of the routing change to avoid partial-state processing.

3) Containment workflow (already aligned with Marissa)
- Snapshot id: pre-prod-20261012 (held for 7 days).
- Thresholds to trigger an emergency pin: >5% drop on accuracy OR any high-severity hallucination on a compliance prompt.
- Execution SLA: 10 minutes to pin + routing switch; ops will notify and open an incident.

4) Scheduling
- Wed 10:30am PT works for us. I’ll send the calendar invite with the Drive + HubSpot links and a short agenda (scorecard review + rollback plan).

Next immediate action items
- PayGrid: upload the 50 priority prompts to the Drive folder today.
- Redwood: we’ll kick the eval runners as soon as they’re uploaded and aim to deliver the initial scorecard within 48 hours.

I’ll also create a HubSpot task for PG-26-014 and attach the eval artifacts there.

Thanks — speak soon,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
